races.name: Yorkshire Dales Distillery/EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes(for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Neverbeatdeswalker
runners_data.note: Finished 9th and 7th in its two runs, both on good — Daniel Tudhope's yard fires on 14-day stats but this runner is trained by Mark Walford (0/9 14-day); a true hold-up type squeezed out of its natural rear position by the density of closers in this field, meaning its effective running style here is compromised.

runners_data.name: Shaniko
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster sends this one out 19 days after a fourth-place finish at 5f on good; hurdling headgear noted — a genuine deep hold-up horse whose four runs include a second at 5f soft, and Daniel Tudhope takes the ride, but its best chance requires a genuine pace to chase, which this race may not supply.

runners_data.name: Mugheer
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke debutant with entirely unknown running style — Burke's 14-day strike rate of 8/43 is among the best in this field, and a first-time runner from this yard in a 5f Catterick maiden is always worth respecting; the big unknown is how Mugheer jumps and whether it shows natural early pace.

runners_data.name: North Coates
runners_data.note: One run to its name, a fifth at 6f good for Michael & David Easterby — stepped down to 5f here, which could sharpen its chance, though it is a natural hold-up horse whose position on the map understates how deep it is likely to race; Billy Garritty takes the ride with the stable at 2/37 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Redrosecastana
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse that fades in the finish, with a single run showing a ninth at 6f good — stepping down to 5f may mask the fade, but Christopher Kellett's 0/3 14-day record and a maiden mark of 120 OR on limited evidence makes assessment difficult; best viewed as a pace-influence rather than a winning candidate.

runners_data.name: Romidijo
runners_data.note: The most experienced runner in the field with six starts — two seconds at 5f and 6f good, plus placed form on good-to-soft — Charlie Clover's charge is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield but arguably the most consistent closer in the race, and 5/7 runs in similar going underpins its adaptability.

runners_data.name: Scottys Rocket
runners_data.note: Like Redrosecastana, flagged as a fader — a single ninth at 5f good for Brian Ellison is limited evidence, but the fade tag at 5f is concerning; Andrew Mullen rides for a yard at 2/26 over 14 days, and this runner may play a role in setting pace before emptying.

runners_data.name: Ghazalia
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Hilal Kobeissi — a trainer with just one 14-day runner — so essentially a complete unknown quantity; Sean D Bowen is a capable jockey who adds some faith, and if Ghazalia shows natural early pace the hold-up-heavy field could be vulnerable to a front-running newcomer.

runners_data.name: Purrista
runners_data.note: Two runs both at 5f good — a third and an eleventh — with the placed effort showing she handles the trip and surface; Gemma Tutty's 0/8 14-day record is modest, but Connor Beasley's jockeyship is a plus, and a horse with genuine placed form at this course-distance-going combination has a legitimate profile for this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner 5f maiden at Catterick, this race lacks any horse with a genuine established lead habit — the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in profile, meaning the early gallop is likely to be modest and contested rather than controlled by a single pace-setter. Neverbeatdeswalker, North Coates, Shaniko, and Romidijo are all true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map simply because the rear is oversubscribed; none of them is likely to secure their natural position or dictate terms. Mugheer and Ghazalia are debutants whose early behaviour is unknown, and any uncontested forward move from either could shape the race entirely. With the pace likely to be muddled and the sprint kicking in earnest from halfway, this race shape strongly favours horses with tactical flexibility — those who can sit handy without needing to be covered up deep — over true deep closers who will find themselves in a bunched field with nowhere to go late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If no horse asserts early and the field drifts into a compact sprint finish from the halfway point.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn gallop compresses the field, and horses who are able to travel just off the non-existent pace find themselves in the perfect position to pounce; Romidijo's consistent placed form at 5-6f good ground makes her the type to capitalise on this shape, and Purrista's placed run at 5f good suggests she handles the trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Breaks Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Mugheer or Ghazalia (or both) show natural early pace on debut and establish an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: A K.R. Burke debutant with unknown style (Mugheer) or the Hilal Kobeissi first-timer (Ghazalia) exploits the hold-up-heavy field by bowling to the front unchallenged; a soft early lead at Catterick's 5f with good ground would suit a genuine front-runner and allow them to control the tempo and hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sprinters Land
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is quick enough to create a proper finish and the back-markers get a clear run.
scenarios.body: Neverbeatdeswalker or Shaniko, both tagged as redistributed true hold-up types, would need everything to fall right — a fast enough gallop, a clean passage, and a short enough gap to close — all less likely given their style_fit discount in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Faders Set Pace, Tire
scenarios.trigger: If Redrosecastana or Scottys Rocket go hard early (as their fade-tagged profiles suggest they might) and set a genuine pace before dying.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop burns off the pace-setters in the final furlong, and a horse sitting second or third — Romidijo or Purrista — who avoids the early burn swoops late to take advantage of the weakening leaders.

watchPoints.text: Watch Mugheer and Ghazalia at the start — if either debutant shows natural early pace and breaks smartly, they could dictate an uncontested lead in a hold-up-dominated field that has no confirmed front-runner to push back.

Romidijo's redistribution from hold-up to midfield on the map means its run style is partially compromised — watch whether Sam James can find a clear path in a bunched finish, as interference risk is high with several hold-up types competing for late room.

Redrosecastana and Scottys Rocket are both tagged as faders at 5f on good ground — if either sets a brief early pace they could burn themselves out and leave the field bunched, creating a chaotic sprint finish where draw and position at halfway becomes decisive.

Shaniko carries headgear (h) and Daniel Tudhope's experience could help it overcome the style-fit penalty — watch whether Tudhope parks it closer than its natural position suggests, given the lack of genuine pace in this race.

North Coates drops from 6f to 5f for the first time — watch whether the trip shortening brings improvement, or whether the Easterby hold-up profile means it needs more race than 5f at Catterick naturally provides.

races.name: Berber Leather Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: Moderate claimer Faye McManoman partners this 4-year-old for a yard with no wins from six in the past fortnight; in truth a genuine hold-up horse whose tendency to fade in finishes is well documented, and being pushed into a midfield map position rather than the rear suits nobody — treat with significant caution.

runners_data.name: Khanimambo
runners_data.note: David Nolan takes the ride for David & Nicola Barron on a 3-year-old with just one run to its name, finishing seventh over this 7f trip on good ground; the lofty opening OR of 120 hints the stable fancies its ability, and 18 days between runs suggests a straightforward prep — the unknown quantity here.

runners_data.name: Skewsby
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty partners this Michael & David Easterby-trained 3-year-old with no racecourse form visible and an unknown style — entirely opaque, and the Easterby yard's 2/37 fortnight strike rate is not a confidence boost, but lightly-raced unknown types can surprise on debut.

runners_data.name: Dreamadera
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends out this hold-up 3-year-old after a lengthy 123-day absence, with form of 12th and 7th on the only two starts suggesting it has work to do; Duran Fentiman rides and the step up from 6f may help, but returning from a long layoff into a contested-pace race is a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this confirmed front-runner who has placed three times on good ground and has strong course-suitability credentials; she will fight Royale Union for the lead, and the key question is whether she burns herself out in that battle or manages to control it — her second at 7f on good is the form to highlight.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Melody
runners_data.note: Donald McCain sends out this 3-year-old for David Allan after a 46-day break, with three runs showing a consistent mid-division pattern; its natural home is at the rear of the field, but the crowded hold-up section means it will likely race further forward than ideal, which blunts the effectiveness of any late effort.

runners_data.name: Royale Union
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's yard is in strong form (8/43 over 14 days) and Clifford Lee takes the ride on this confirmed front-runner who placed over this exact trip on good ground; if he can assert over Lady Gormire early without burning too many matches, the tactical picture is genuinely interesting from the front.

runners_data.name: Soca Star
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's 3-year-old has been placed seven times from twelve outings on good ground and is a consistent prominent racer whose profile fits a contested-pace 7f perfectly; Dale Swift rides after just 8 days since the last run, suggesting the horse is fit and ready, and the form figures of 2nd and 3rd show it knows how to finish.

races.paceDynamic: Royale Union and Lady Gormire are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over Catterick's 7f, creating a genuine contested pace rather than a dawdle. With two horses fighting for the same position, the gallop should be honest and sustained, stretching the field and potentially setting up those who can travel just off the pace. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Moonlight Melody and Aurora's Doublesix are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield positions they are unlikely to secure naturally, meaning their finishing kicks may be compromised if they cannot get back to their ideal spot. Prominent and close-tracking profiles (Soca Star, Khanimambo) who can sit just behind the battle for the lead without expending energy are best placed tactically, as a contested pace at 7f on good ground at Catterick should reward those who travel smoothly into contention rather than deep closers forced to make up ground from further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Royale Union and Lady Gormire fight for the front and set an honest, pressured gallop that softens both leaders in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The duel between Royale Union and Lady Gormire burns both horses up, leaving the race to those who track efficiently just off the pace and pick up the pieces; this shape is Soca Star's ideal setup, having shown consistent prominent-to-midfield form on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Royale Union successfully shakes off Lady Gormire early and is allowed to dictate a controlled, even gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner setting its own terms through Catterick's 7f on good ground can be very hard to reel in, and Royale Union's recent placed form at this trip on good ground supports the profile; Connor Beasley on Lady Gormire will be the key aggressor to watch, but if she fades from the contest Royale Union may get a soft lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel fizzles out rather than setting a true gallop and the race becomes a sprint from the turn.
scenarios.body: In this shape, horses with a turn of foot in the final furlong benefit, and Khanimambo — despite just one run — enters with a lofty opening mark suggesting a yard that expects a serious performance; Moonlight Melody, though mapped to midfield from a true hold-up position, would theoretically benefit here but its style-fit concern and limited form cap confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Rank Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is chaotic, the field spreads wide, and an unconventional or lightly-raced runner exploits the confusion.
scenarios.body: Skewsby is entirely unknown on style and form, and Michael & David Easterby have a debutant or near-debutant who could produce a raw but unpenalised performance at a generous price; Aurora's Doublesix is a genuine hold-up horse forced forward by redistribution and would only feature if a truly exceptional late run materialises, which its recent fade record makes unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Royale Union and Lady Gormire — watch the first two furlongs to see which of the two front-runners gains the upper hand; if neither concedes early, the pace could be unsustainably hot and set up Soca Star for a decisive late strike.

Moonlight Melody and Aurora's Doublesix — both are genuine hold-up horses who cannot get to their natural rear positions in this field; if either ends up racing prominently against their instincts, their finishing efforts are likely to be blunted.
Khanimambo — David Nolan on a yard's lightly-raced runner with an OR of 120 on just one start is a classic "stable knows something" profile; watch for unusual support in the market before post time.

Skewsby — completely unknown style and no visible form; Billy Garritty's instructions from the Easterby yard will shape where this runner slots in, and a surprise showing from an unconventional position cannot be ruled out in a field of maidens with this much uncertainty.

Dreamadera — returning from 123 days off for Tim Easterby into a hot-paced race; fitness after a long absence is a genuine concern, and any signs of greenness or sluggishness early would confirm this is a run-into-form outing rather than a winning bid.

races.name: Happy 50th Birthday Victoria Melling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Run This Way
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old prominent runner with genuine 6f Good-ground form — two wins at this trip in recent history — and David Nolan is a strong booking; 81 days off is the main query but Paul Midgley's 2-from-16 T14 strike rate suggests the yard is not firing at peak, making the layoff worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Run This Way carries 135 lb from stall three on familiar distance and going; our rating of 70 heads the field, and the 81-day absence is the one query.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride on this hold-up 7-year-old who has been campaigned at 7-8f recently and whose sole turf 6f run this season produced a well-beaten tenth; the step back down in trip against speedier rivals is a genuine concern and her Good-ground record (11th most recent similar-going run) offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Miss Willows was beaten well last time, and three of her last five runs make for grim reading, with only a second two starts back offering any encouragement; ranked fifth of six on our figures, she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old has a strong 6f Good-ground profile with two wins at this trip in recent form, and the p-headgear (presumably a hood or cheekpieces) has been a feature on a horse running into form; David Allan is an experienced northern jockey who knows this circuit, and 9 days since last run is an entirely fresh book for this yard.
runners_data.comment: Barmyblade won three starts back and won again two starts before that, showing he retains the ability to threaten at this level, and he has experience of today's distance and going with a quick turnaround of just nine days; the concern is a trainer operating at just 3% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Overbudget
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed pace-setter whose style fit is flagged at 0.93, meaning this is effectively racing into its natural role at the front — the concern is that a record of 0 wins from 8 similar-going runs at 6f and a form string of 283769 suggests it has been used as a pace-setter without converting, making it a race-shaper rather than race-winner.

runners_data.name: Powernap
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by history who is mapped to midfield here only because the rear is over-subscribed with closers; its best form has come on Soft ground (one win) and on 5f, and while it has placed twice at 6f on Good, the positional squeeze and Dougie Costello needing to find space late on makes this harder than it looks on figures alone.
runners_data.comment: Powernap showed her class when winning two starts back, and seconds on two of her other recent efforts underline her consistency; she has run over today's trip and going, and draws stall one carrying 130 lb. The eighth last time out after 48 days off is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a solid recent form string including placed efforts at 6f on Good ground and a course win at this distance, but Jason Hart will find its hold-up inclinations difficult to satisfy when Powernap and Miss Willows occupy the same rear position — the redistribution means it is unlikely to travel in its preferred slot, tempering its chance despite the appealing profile.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Battenburg Belle faces a stiff task, though she has experience over today's distance and going and arrives on a reasonable turnaround of 22 days, with two thirds in her last two starts suggesting she retains some consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Overbudget is the lone confirmed front runner in this six-runner 6f handicap and, critically, faces no serious pressure for the lead — this is a sustainable, uncontested gallop rather than a hot-pace scenario. Run This Way will push forward from the prominent style to sit just behind, but neither horse is likely to force a breakneck tempo, meaning the early fractions should be controlled and honest rather than fierce. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate: Powernap and Battenburg Belle are genuine closers by profile but have been mapped forward because the rear of the field is congested with similar styles, and neither is likely to secure their natural position with ease. This race shape — a solo leader setting a measured pace over a flat 6f on Good ground — strongly favours prominent and just-off-the-pace runners who can track within striking range and produce a finish, rather than true deep closers who will need an unlikely collapse in the front end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Overbudget Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Overbudget sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo and the race is run at a steady-to-honest pace that rewards those sitting close.
scenarios.body: Overbudget dictates from the front with no rival willing to pressurise, and horses like Run This Way who sit prominently just behind get the perfect stalking position entering the final 2f. Good ground on a flat track amplifies this shape as front-end energy is preserved, giving the lead-tracking runners first run on the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Collapse, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than it looks and Overbudget burns its fuel, opening a gap for hold-up types to rattle home.
scenarios.body: Overbudget over-commits in front and begins to tie up inside the final furlong, leaving a window for genuine closers to cut through. However, Powernap and Battenburg Belle face positional disadvantage given the crowded hold-up section, making this scenario materially harder to execute than it appears on paper.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel, Frontrunner Outstayed
scenarios.trigger: If Run This Way pressures Overbudget aggressively from early on, forcing a genuine early pace battle.
scenarios.body: The two prominent horses race against each other through the early stages, raising the tempo and creating a more searching gallop than expected, which begins to suit runners coming from slightly further back. Barmyblade, with proven form at 6f on Good ground and multiple course-distance wins, is ideally placed to benefit from a pace-injected race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, Form Horse Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the race lacks rhythm entirely due to hesitation or positional shuffling among the hold-up pack, and one horse with superior class asserts.
scenarios.body: A messy, slow-burning race with little meaningful pace ends up suiting the most class-consistent performer to simply outgrind rivals in the closing stages. This is the least structured scenario and the hardest to predict, with no single horse holding a decisive positional or ability edge to exploit chaos cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Overbudget's sectionals through the first 2f are critical — if it sets a stronger gallop than expected under no pressure, the race may evolve very differently from a controlled-pace shape.
Powernap and Battenburg Belle may obstruct each other early doors if both attempt to settle in the same region of the field — watch for traffic interference or a crowded rear section developing.

Run This Way's 81-day absence for a yard running at 2/16 over 14 days is a live flag — if it shows any sluggishness leaving the stalls, its prominent style becomes harder to execute and its chance evaporates quickly.

Barmyblade's headgear (p) should be confirmed at the declaration stage — if it is a first-time application or a recent addition to a horse with improving form, it may represent a larger move forward than the handicapper has priced in.

Good ground is confirmed for this race by the going report and all key fancied runners carry OK going flags, so no surface-based deflection is expected — the race should run true to pace shape rather than being distorted by unexpected underfoot conditions.

races.name: Hats Of Yorkshire Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: A lightly-burdened hold-up stayer for Donald McCain who has placed at 1m6f twice on Good ground recently; David Nolan's positive association with the trip and going are the main angles, and the 39-day break looks inconsequential given clear fitness markers in recent form.
runners_data.comment: Animato is winless in his last five starts but showed glimpses of promise with a third last time out, and he has run over today's distance and going before; our rating of 65 puts him clear at the head of this field, and 39 days between runs looks a fair freshener.

runners_data.name: Zephlyn
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans runner who carries solid similar-going form (2W3P) at this exact course and trip, redistributed to the front as the only pace source in the race — racing sharply out of role, so a STYLE_FIT discount applies, but the course-and-distance experience is a genuine positive.
runners_data.comment: Zephlyn has run over today's trip and going and, carrying 137 lb off an official mark of 54, a placing three starts back hints at ability worth respecting, with our rating edging his official figure; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and struggles to build on that promise.

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who finds himself pushed forward into a midfield mapping due to the field's density of closers; Connor Beasley's tactical judgment will matter here, and the horse's 0W0P record at similar distances tempers confidence despite the slight reprieve in grade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mr Withington at least has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 15 days between runs leaves him fresh; however, carrying 132 lb on a modest official mark of 49 makes life tough for a horse who has not threatened the frame in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Niffler
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's lightly-raced three-year-old with a recent win over 1m2f at Southwell, stepping up sharply in trip — the ⚠ fade flag is the key concern at 1m6f, though Prescott's meticulous placing record means the step up may be more considered than it appears; Luke Morris should position forward from the midfield mapping.
runners_data.comment: Niffler won last time out and has a trainer firing at 30% in the past fortnight, though three of his last four starts produced unplaced or poor finishes and the quick six-day turnaround is worth watching under 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Fairydale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has placed twice at 1m2f on Good ground and holds headgear (visor) that may sharpen her focus; though naturally a hold-up type squeezed into midfield, her two recent placed efforts on turf suggest she handles Good conditions, and David Allan's local knowledge is an asset.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Fairydale faces a stiff ask, with her trainer in poor form at 3% over the past fortnight; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a second two starts back offers a crumb of hope.

runners_data.name: This Rib
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this David Loughnane three-year-old who has only placed once in seven similar-going runs and whose recent form string includes a pull-up — a genuine hold-up horse sitting in midfield by necessity rather than preference, and the limited similar-going record (3 runs) makes confidence hard to build.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, This Rib nonetheless rates as a clear danger here, our figures putting him a cut above most rivals, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is a pulled up effort in recent form.

runners_data.name: Manbearpig
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' three-year-old has a tidy record at 1m4f-1m6f on Good ground with four placed efforts in that window; a natural hold-up type nudged forward on the map, Faleh Bughanaim rides, and the 11-day turnaround is short but the trainer's 0/10 in the 14-day window invites mild caution.
runners_data.comment: Manbearpig has run over today's trip and going before and shaped with promise when fourth last time out and fourth three starts back, suggesting the current mark of 50 may be workable; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts and must find improvement to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Lilykoy
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's three-year-old has a most recent run of 3rd over 1m6f on Good ground at Catterick itself — the strongest course-and-distance angle in the field; Alex Jary takes the 3lb claim which helps at the bottom of the weights, and as a hold-up type mapped forward, proximity to the pace on the final turn could be decisive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lilykoy is hard to fancy at the weights, though she has run over today's going before and her third last time out at least shows she can get into the frame on her day.

races.paceDynamic: Zephlyn is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 1m6f Catterick handicap and, despite being a natural prominent-to-hold-up type redistributed to the front, is the most likely horse to establish early fractions — meaning the race is expected to be run at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a genuine searching pace. With no other horse likely to challenge for the lead, the tempo should be modest and even, creating a race that sets up for those with tactical speed rather than pure stayers who need a hard, grinding test. The absence of pressure on Zephlyn means the field will likely bunch and travel in a compact group through the early stages, with the race only truly igniting inside the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or make a forward move from midfield on the turn, as a slow-to-moderate pace at 1m6f on Good ground at Catterick rewards those with a turn of foot over pure relentless galloping ability. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Fairydale, This Rib, Manbearpig, Mr Withington, and Lilykoy are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield, meaning only one or two will actually secure a truly forward position and benefit from proximity to the controlled pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zephlyn Controls, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Zephlyn sets an uncontested moderate pace and the race develops into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Zephlyn's solo lead at a comfortable tempo means the field travels in a pack and the race becomes a flat-out dash home, rewarding any horse with residual acceleration stepping out of midfield on the final bend; on Good ground at Catterick the turn into the straight can be decisive for those positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Midfield Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one horse tracks Zephlyn slightly closer than the rest and delivers a sustained run from the two-furlong pole to score.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield means the horse who secures the best position on Zephlyn's quarters — likely the one whose jockey is most aggressive on the turn — has first run on those wider or further back; a controlled early pace means that horse's energy is preserved perfectly for a sustained late effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Zephlyn Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate, uncontested pace proves so sustainable that Zephlyn quickens away before the field can respond.
scenarios.body: Whilst racing out of natural role, Zephlyn does hold solid course form at 1m6f on Good ground and with 2W3P on similar going, a well-judged front-running display could see the field leave it too late to close; a STYLE_FIT discount applies but the scenario is not impossible at this level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up significantly mid-race and the true hold-up horses get the searching gallop they need to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a meaningful increase in tempo that the current race shape does not support, and most genuine closers here are compressed into midfield rather than racing in their natural rearward position, reducing their ability to deliver a true late swoop; only if the race fragments and splits apart does a hold-up winner become realistic.

watchPoints.text: Lilykoy's course-and-distance third at Catterick is the standout positional clue — watch whether Alex Jary (3lb claim) moves forward early on the turn to capitalise on the compressed midfield before the others can react.

Zephlyn setting an uncontested, very slow pace risks the race turning into a sprint for a horse that is not a natural front-runner — monitor how comfortably Jason Hart can hold the position without over-extending Zephlyn before the straight.

Niffler carries a fade flag in the finish and is making a sharp step up to 1m6f from 1m2f — if the pace is genuinely slow, the final climb at Catterick could expose the stamina question severely in the closing stages.

With six of eight runners compressed into midfield, the draw and early positioning from the stalls will be disproportionately important — any horse that breaks sharply and secures a forward berth on the rail heading to the far turn gains a structural advantage over those stuck wide in traffic.

Tim Easterby's T14 return of 3/94 is healthy volume but undistinguished by strike-rate — Fairydale's visor application and Good-ground placed form are the genuine angles to monitor rather than trainer form alone.

races.name: Oops A Daisy Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fidelius
runners_data.note: Consistent front-of-field performer on Good ground at five furlongs with two places in fifteen similar-going runs, trained by Nigel Tinkler whose 14-day strike rate is modest (1/20) but this horse's form holds up well fresh at 18 days; sits right in the pocket behind Secret Mistral and is the textbook profile for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Fidelius shaped with real promise when second last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 94 puts him firmly in the picture from stall six; the concern is a trainer operating at just 5% in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Marching Mac
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's hold-up specialist returns after 75 days off — the layoff is a concern — but his single Good-ground win came over this exact trip and the trainer/jockey combination is in-house, suggesting they know the horse's readiness; needs pace to quicken off.
runners_data.comment: Marching Mac won on his most recent start and has experience of both today's trip and going conditions, making him an appealing fit here; a 75-day absence is worth noting, but that recent win gives him solid claims from stall eight off 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: Recent runner (5 days ago) for Michael & David Easterby, prominent style, and two wins and two places in fifteen Good-ground starts suggest he handles conditions; the very quick turnaround after just five days is the key question mark, though trainer's 14-day strike rate is active (2/37).
runners_data.comment: Canon's House shaped with plenty of promise when third three starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; ranked top of the field on our ratings, the concern is a trainer currently in the grip of a cold spell.

runners_data.name: Novamay
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Michael Dods who has a strong 13-from-15 record at getting horses placed on Good ground — the best trainer stat in this field — though his five recent runs have all been at six furlongs, making the drop to five a genuine stamina question in reverse; jockey Rhys Elliott takes a 5lb claim.
runners_data.comment: Novamay won three starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of just 15 days, bringing experience of today's distance and going and an 89 rating that marks her out as a live threat from stall three; the risk is that her two most recent efforts were a sixth and an eighth.

runners_data.name: Secret Mistral
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner and the pivot around which the whole shape turns; Tony Carroll's six-year-old has won and placed multiple times on Good ground over five furlongs recently and faces a five-pound claimer in Myla Coppins, though the lack of a pace rival means she can nurse her lead without burning energy.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Secret Mistral brings solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going, but carrying 136 lb from stall seven and a speed rating below her official mark suggest she faces a stiff task to go one better.

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Ruth Carr who has won back-to-back recently on Good ground at five furlongs (form 110), giving her live each-way claims; 14 days since last run is straightforward, and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim helps at the weights.
runners_data.comment: Angel Numbers was unplaced last time out, which is hard to ignore, and she ranks eighth of ten on our figures; however, she was a winner two starts back and three starts back, showing she retains ability, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has struggled badly in recent starts (form 00 last two), and while her natural style is hold-up, she sits in midfield on this map because the rear is congested with closers — racing outside her optimal position further tempers already modest recent form.
runners_data.comment: A second four starts back shows she has ability, but three subsequent efforts — two unplaced runs the latest — raise questions; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 132 lb from stall 4, and a rating of 86 suggests some residual class to call on.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old runs in a tongue tie and blinkers (hg:tb) and comes back quickly at 11 days; a true hold-up horse whose best efforts on Good ground came at five furlongs but who, displaced from the rear by a crowded closer's pack, will struggle to replicate that position — David Allan can only do so much.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with an unplaced effort 11 days ago and a trainer in notably poor form at 3%, Vince L'Amour is hard to fancy from stall ten carrying 126 lb; experience over today's trip and going is at least something in his favour.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides for Tristan Davidson, whose small yard is in a productive 14-day window (3/8); the eight-year-old has two wins and three places from fifteen Good-ground runs and won last time out over this course and distance — his prominent style suits the likely shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Opened his recent account with a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but his form is inconsistent — ninth two starts back — and 126 lb from stall 9 adds to the challenge for a horse rated just 67 officially.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old wears a hood (hg:p), ran nine days ago, and has two wins and seven places in fifteen Good-ground efforts — a rock-solid place record; prominent style fits, but her best recent form has come over six furlongs, and the five-furlong requirement at pace may catch her in the final strides.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and representing a trainer in poor form at just 3%, Canaria Queen faces a stiff ask here, though she has experience of today's trip and conditions, was second last time out, and stall one is hers from 123 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Mistral is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she should slot into an uncontested position on the stands rail and dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good turf at Catterick's flat five furlongs. Behind her, Fidelius, Canon's House, Our Absent Friends, and Canaria Queen all want prominent positions, creating meaningful congestion in the two-to-four lengths band from two furlongs out where the race will be won or lost. Marching Mac, Angel Numbers, and Novamay are the legitimate hold-up threats, but their challenge depends entirely on whether the early tempo is brisk enough to stretch the field and expose those racing prominently. Because Call Margot and Vince L'Amour are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield due to the density of closers — with Call Margot and Vince L'Amour both unlikely to find their natural rear-of-field position — the race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track Secret Mistral at close quarters and pounce from two furlongs out, particularly those with proven form on Good ground at five furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Mistral dictates an honest but sustainable gallop and the prominent pack tracks closely, setting up a straight-line battle from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Secret Mistral's uncontested lead becomes a tempo-setter rather than a race-winner, and the prominent horses who travel smoothly behind her — particularly Fidelius, Canon's House, and Our Absent Friends — are ideally placed to strike as the field fans out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack fails to exert enough pressure and Secret Mistral's controlled lead is never genuinely threatened, allowing her to coast home.
scenarios.body: Secret Mistral has an excellent recent record on Good ground at five furlongs — winning and placing in both disciplines — and an uncontested lead at Catterick can prove decisive when rivals get into each other's way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group burns each other off through congestion and traffic, leaving a gap for a genuine hold-up horse to finish powerfully through.
scenarios.body: Marching Mac and Angel Numbers are the most credible hold-up threats with authentic finishing form, and if the four prominent runners crowd and impede each other between two and three furlongs out, a clear late run becomes available.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Plays Into Outsider Hands
scenarios.trigger: If stall exits are uneven, the prominent group clashes early, and a runner finds an unexpected clear passage on either rail.
scenarios.body: At Catterick's flat five furlongs a messy break can neutralise class advantages quickly, and runners like Novamay or Canaria Queen — both showing recent course-and-distance form — could benefit from a scrambled pace pattern.

watchPoints.text: Secret Mistral (front-runner, Myla Coppins 5lb claim) — if Coppins is unable to find and hold the rail early, the lone leader loses her key tactical advantage and the race shape collapses entirely.

Prominent congestion between Canon's House, Fidelius, Our Absent Friends, and Canaria Queen is the central traffic hazard — watch for interference two to three furlongs out as all four angle for the same ground on a narrow Catterick straight.

Our Absent Friends (Jason Hart, Tristan Davidson yard in form) — recent course-and-distance win combined with prominent style makes him a sharp positional threat; if Hart gets a clean passage on the outside of the prominent group he bypasses the traffic danger entirely.

Marching Mac's 75-day absence is the field's longest layoff — watch for signs of rustiness in the market or in early movement, as a below-par return from such a break would remove the most credible late-run option.

Call Margot and Vince L'Amour are unlikely to find their natural hold-up positions and will race closer to the pace than ideal — monitor whether they create unexpected interference for the prominent group rather than contributing as genuine closers.

races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Bizarre Law
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up operator with a win and a placed run on similar Going in recent history; has been operating at 8f lately so dropping back to 7f is a slight concern, and with so many hold-up types in this field, finding its natural rearmost berth will be difficult — likely to be closer than usual to the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Bizarre Law won four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving him solid claims on conditions; carrying 135 lb from stall nine after 49 days off is the concern.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and the key pace-maker for the whole race; best form clusters on 5-6f on Good ground, so this 7f trip on Good could test stamina if it goes too hard, though an uncontested lead gives it every chance to control fractions and stay fresh.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but consistently competitive, Golden Prosperity brings vital experience over today's trip and conditions, and that runner-up finish last time out — just 19 days ago — signals he arrives in good nick carrying 135 lb from stall two; the worry is he has yet to convert that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: I Can Boogy
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who typically holds up but has been placed at 7-8f on Southwell's AW and turf; no wins in 15 Good-ground starts is a significant red flag, and being pushed into a midfield slot in a field loaded with similar types makes its task harder.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a third three starts back, suggest I Can Boogy is threatening to find her form, and our rating of 55 gives her a case from stall one carrying 135 lb; the main concern is a trainer in a cold spell at just 5% over the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who naturally wants to be close to the pace and is one of only two runners who can realistically press Golden Prosperity; consistent placed form at 6f on Good suggests the trip is a stretch, but if it can slot in second or third the race is set up perfectly for its style.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a runner-up six starts back, Mister Sky Blue brings solid recent form into this, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead; yet to win in his last six starts, but our rating of 60 makes him the one to beat from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Moral Victory
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with just three runs in the form book and a worrying tendency to fade in the finish; pushed into a midfield berth by the volume of hold-up types, and with two placings out of three runs coming on Southwell's AW, the Good turf looks a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Moral Victory faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and 34 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but an official rating of 36 makes him hard to fancy against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with a win and five placings in 15 Good-ground starts, suggesting it finds the going consistently but rarely wins; holds up naturally and will need the pace to collapse late to get involved, making it one of the more credible deep closers in the field.|

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with two second-place finishes in last five runs including a 2nd at 7f on Soft, suggesting the trip and easing ground are not a problem; naturally a hold-up type who produces consistent placed form — a horse to respect if the race sets up for late runners.|
runners_data.comment: Ridgemaster arrives here second last time out and is yet to win in his last six starts, with a pair of sevenths in that sequence tempering the promise of two placed efforts; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 135 lb from stall 10, the weight is the notable query.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran whose best recent result is a 2nd at 7f on Good, directly relevant form for this contest; holds up and needs the pace to be genuine to arrive late — on this track with a slow-burning front-runner, getting into the race from the rear will be the challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts but placed twice in that spell, Without Delay has run over today's trip and going and steps back into contention off 135 lb from stall six; a second last time out offers encouragement, though consistency remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Belling The Cat
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with placed form at 6-7f on Good ground, carrying a 5lb age allowance against the older horses; a genuine hold-up type whose form figures suggest mid-pack finishes rather than wins, and the redistribution into a midfield position means it will be racing in a crowd rather than from its preferred rearmost position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Belling The Cat faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and arrives reasonably fresh on 32 days' rest from stall five carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Dee's Honey
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a string of 9th-place finishes on Good ground and a noted tendency to fade late — the form figures make it very difficult to make a case here regardless of race shape, and Good turf at 7f has not been kind in recent outings.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a pair of ninth-place finishes in her two most recent outings, Dee's Honey faces a stiff task ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, though she has run over today's trip and returns after just 12 days off.

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with consecutive 2nd and 3rd placings in its last two starts on Good ground at 6f, showing it is in decent form at OR 48; holds up naturally but is one of those squeezed out of its preferred rear position by the volume of hold-up types — if it can get closer to the pace than usual, the recent form is respectable.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lanarra does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 18 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but a mark of 48 and a midfield ranking among 13 rivals underline the size of the task from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Runninman
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who holds up but has struggled for form on softer and artificial surfaces; last ran just 7 days ago and wears a tongue tie and hood, suggesting the trainer is searching for the right conditions — Good turf at 7f is a new test and the recent heavy workload may count against it.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked eleventh of thirteen on our figures, Runninman faces a stiff ask here; a fourth three starts back offers a sliver of encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but the weight of 130 lb from stall eight adds further pressure.

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a finish-fading flag and a form string that shows 7th, 10th and 8th in three of its last four outings on Good ground; the form does not inspire confidence, and on a track where the pace will be controlled, a horse that fades in the straight has a very narrow path to relevance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ryefield at least steps back up to familiar distance and going conditions, and 14 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a sequence of sevenths and eighths makes it hard to see him reversing that slide from stall three off 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Twilight Dawn
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with back-to-back 3rd-place finishes on Good ground at 7f, which is the most directly relevant recent form in the field; wears a hood and naturally wants to be held up, but the redistribution means it will be racing in a midfield group — if it can find a clean run, the 7f Good form makes it one to note.|
runners_data.comment: Twilight Dawn has placed third on two occasions in recent starts and has run over today's trip and conditions before, but she is yet to win in her last five outings and an unplaced effort last time out is a concern from stall 12 off 130 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Golden Prosperity is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to take them on from the front, should be able to dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop across Catterick's flat seven furlongs. The pace is unlikely to be truly strong — one horse setting fractions at its own tempo on Good ground historically compresses the finish and keeps the leader fresh into the straight. The bulk of this field are hold-up or midfield types by nature, though Lanarra, Bizarre Law, Twilight Dawn and others have been redistributed on the map because the field contains more genuine hold-up horses than there are rear positions to fill — Mister Sky Blue and Golden Prosperity are the most likely to actually secure prominent berths, with Bizarre Law perhaps able to slot in closer than its natural style suggests. This shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter on a flat track with a moderate gallop — firmly favours horses who can track the leader through the middle stages and quicken from a prominent or close-tracking position rather than true closers, who will face a wall of horses in a compressed finish with limited room to motor through from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Golden Prosperity Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity is allowed to roll along at a comfortable solo fractions and nothing in the field has the desire or position to challenge for the front.
scenarios.body: Golden Prosperity sets a manageable pace and, with the race on its terms, simply refuses to come back to the field in the straight on Good ground; the horse's best form at 6f on Good suggests stamina is not a given at 7f, but an uncontested lead is a powerful compensator. Prominent horses who can track and pounce — particularly Mister Sky Blue — are best placed to capitalise if the leader ties up, while true hold-up types will find traffic in a compressed finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity sets the pace but visibly ties up in the final furlong, allowing a prominent tracking horse to pick it off.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest enough to stretch Golden Prosperity, and a horse sitting just a length or two off the pace in second or third can coast into contention without needing to find an extra gear from too far back. Mister Sky Blue's consistent placed form on Good ground and Ridgemaster's two second-place finishes at similar distances make them natural beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and backmarkers find a clean, unimpeded run through the field in a compressed finish.
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop dictated by Golden Prosperity could ironically cause a concertina effect in the straight if several horses quicken simultaneously, creating a brief gap for a hold-up horse with a strong late stride to exploit. Rain Cap and Without Delay both have placed form on Good going at 7f and represent the most credible genuine closers in this field, though both must avoid traffic in what will be a busy straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity goes too slowly and the whole field converges in the final furlong with no single horse able to assert.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop could bring every horse into contention simultaneously, turning the race into a sprint finish where OR ratings are compressed and the result becomes near-random. In this scenario, horses with the highest OR and best recent form — Ridgemaster and Without Delay — have a marginal class edge over the field, though no runner stands out clearly.

watchPoints.text: Golden Prosperity — watch whether it is allowed to bowl along uncontested from the gate or if Mister Sky Blue pressures it early; an untroubled lead is the linchpin of the dominant race shape and any early battle fundamentally changes how this race is run.

Mister Sky Blue — watch its position at the start; if it slots in second or third tracking Golden Prosperity it becomes the most naturally advantaged horse in the race, but if it gets shuffled back into the midfield pack its chance diminishes sharply.

Twilight Dawn and Lanarra — both have the most relevant recent form (consecutive 3rds on Good at 7f) but are likely to be riding in a congested midfield rather than their preferred positions; a clean, unimpeded run to the rail in the straight is critical for either to land a blow.

Rain Cap and Without Delay — both are veteran hold-up types with placed form on Good ground at 7f, and if Golden Prosperity sets too slow a pace and then sprints clear, these two are the most likely to be left with too much ground to make up in the final furlong.|
